answer.text: the part of the deficit caused only by a recession
the deficit that would remain even if the economy were at its normal level of output

questiontext.text: Automatic stabilisers are

generalfeedback.text: In a boom, income-tax revenue rises and unemployment benefits fall, which withdraws spending. In a slump the opposite happens.

answer.text: tax and benefit rules that reduce the amplitude of the business cycle without a new policy decision
discretionary changes announced in each budget
tariffs that change every week by ministerial order

questiontext.text: Crowding in occurs when

generalfeedback.text: Roads, ports or a more secure outlook can complement private projects. Crowding out is the opposite interest-rate or resource effect.

answer.text: public investment raises the profitability of private investment, so private investment rises
public borrowing necessarily cuts private investment one for one at full employment

questiontext.text: Fiscal policy uses

generalfeedback.text: The budget is the fiscal instrument. Monetary policy uses the money supply and interest rates.

questiontext.text: A government wants to reduce demand-pull inflation. A suitable fiscal action is

generalfeedback.text: Contractionary fiscal policy reduces aggregate demand. Expansion would widen an inflationary gap.

answer.text: buying securities on the open market, which is fiscal policy

raising taxes or cutting government spending

questiontext.text: During a boom, income-tax revenue rises and unemployment benefits fall. This automatic change

generalfeedback.text: The budget moves toward surplus, or a smaller deficit, without anyone voting a new tax. That leakage slows the rise in disposable income.

answer.text: raises the multiplier above its recession value

questiontext.text: Near full employment, a bond-financed rise in government spending is more likely to crowd out private investment if

generalfeedback.text: With little spare capacity and a fixed money supply, extra borrowing pushes up interest rates. In a liquidity trap or a deep slump, that channel is weak.

answer.text: taxes are cut by the same amount and the balanced-budget multiplier is the only effect considered, with interest rates fixed
the money supply does not rise and the interest rate increases
the economy is in a liquidity trap

generalfeedback.text: Borrowing during a year is a flow. The national debt is the stock that results from past borrowing that has not been repaid.

answer.text: stock of debt accumulated over all past years

questiontext.text: Which is expansionary fiscal policy?

generalfeedback.text: Lower taxes or higher spending raise aggregate demand. Higher taxes or lower spending are contractionary.

answer.text: A rise in income tax rates
A cut in capital spending with no other change
A cut in income tax or a rise in government spending on goods and services

questiontext.text: Why might fiscal policy act with a lag?

generalfeedback.text: Recognition, decision and implementation lags mean a stimulus can arrive after the recession has already turned.

answer.text: Tax rates change output on the same morning they are drafted, with no delay

Government spending is not part of aggregate demand

questiontext.text: Speculative demand for money is

Store of value only, with no other function accepted

questiontext.text: An increase in the required reserve ratio is

generalfeedback.text: A higher reserve ratio lowers the deposit multiplier and forces banks to hold more reserves, so lending capacity falls.

answer.text: contractionary, because banks can lend a smaller fraction of deposits

questiontext.text: A common market goes beyond a customs union by allowing

generalfeedback.text: Goods, services, labour and capital can move. An economic union goes further and harmonises economic policy.

answer.text: free movement of factors of production among members
each member to set a different external tariff
only free movement of goods, with labour and capital still blocked

questiontext.text: A customs union is a free-trade area plus

generalfeedback.text: Members liberalise trade among themselves and apply the same tariff to the rest of the world.

answer.text: no rules on trade with outsiders
a common currency and a single central bank, and nothing less

questiontext.text: A free-trade area removes tariffs among members and

generalfeedback.text: The absence of a common external tariff is what separates a free-trade area from a customs union.

answer.text: requires free movement of labour and a common fiscal policy
lets each member keep its own tariff against non-members

questiontext.text: An economic union typically adds, beyond a common market,

generalfeedback.text: Policy coordination is the extra step. A monetary union, with one currency, is a deeper form.

answer.text: the abolition of the common external tariff
harmonised economic policies, and sometimes a common currency

questiontext.text: The CARICOM Single Market and Economy is intended to

generalfeedback.text: CSME is the deepening of CARICOM beyond a simple trade preference, toward a single market. It is not itself a world-trade institution.

answer.text: be a monetary instrument of a single parish council
set the world price of oil
deepen integration among members, including freer movement of goods, services, capital and skills
replace CARICOM with a free-trade area that keeps barriers to factor movement as its goal

questiontext.text: Trade creation in a customs union is

generalfeedback.text: Trade creation is a gain. Trade diversion, the shift from a cheaper non-member to a dearer member because of the common external tariff, is a possible loss.

answer.text: the replacement of higher-cost domestic production by lower-cost imports from a partner
a fall in exports to zero
the replacement of lower-cost imports from outside the union by higher-cost partner imports

questiontext.text: A small member of a customs union may lose if

generalfeedback.text: The welfare effect of joining is the balance of creation and diversion, plus any scale or terms-of-trade effects. Diversion can dominate.

answer.text: trade creation is the only effect and partner costs are lower
the common external tariff is zero on a good it already imported freely from the partner
it specialises according to comparative advantage inside a free-trade area with no diversion

questiontext.text: Before a customs union, St Brice imported cement from the cheapest world supplier. After the union it buys dearer cement from a partner because the common external tariff shuts out the world supplier. This is

generalfeedback.text: The union has diverted trade from a lower-cost outsider to a higher-cost insider. That is trade diversion.

answer.text: a free-trade area with no external tariff

questiontext.text: Which sequence moves from shallower to deeper integration?

generalfeedback.text: Each step adds a commitment: a common external tariff, then factor mobility, then policy harmonisation.

answer.text: Common market, then a free-trade area that reintroduces internal tariffs as a deepening
Customs union, then separate external tariffs as a deepening
Free-trade area, customs union, common market, economic union

a surplus on the capital account
a rise in the domestic birth rate of graduates

generalfeedback.text: A country can grow and still fail to develop if health, schooling and the quality of jobs do not improve.

answer.text: only the rise in nominal GDP

improvements in living standards, such as health and education, and changes in the structure of the economy

questiontext.text: Economic growth means

generalfeedback.text: Growth is a quantity concept, usually measured by the percentage change in real GDP. It is not the same as development.

answer.text: a more equal distribution of a fixed output
any rise in the price level
an increase in real national output over time

questiontext.text: Measurable Economic Welfare, as named in this syllabus, is best understood as

generalfeedback.text: The syllabus uses Measurable Economic Welfare for a welfare-adjusted view of national income. Students are not required to compute the adjustment.

answer.text: the same statistic as the Gini coefficient
an adjustment of a national-income measure for welfare-relevant items such as leisure and environmental costs

questiontext.text: Sustainable development means meeting present needs

generalfeedback.text: The standard definition requires the path of development to be one that future generations can continue.

answer.text: only by maximising this year's nominal GDP
by using up natural resources as fast as possible
without any reference to the environment
without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their needs

answer.text: inflation, unemployment and the budget deficit only
exports, imports and the exchange rate only

answer.text: identical to its income rank, because HDI is GDP
undefined, because education is not in the index
improved by the poor health indicators

generalfeedback.text: The World Bank group lends and advises for development projects and programmes. It is not the WTO and not the IMF.

acting as a country's commercial bank for household deposits

wider markets and access to foreign capital and technology

generalfeedback.text: Capital and demand can leave quickly, and a narrow export base transmits world prices into local income. Those are costs to set against the gains from trade and FDI.

answer.text: greater exposure to external shocks and to footloose capital
an automatic improvement in the terms of trade every year
a smaller market for every export, by definition
the inability to import goods that the country cannot produce

questiontext.text: A tariff is

questiontext.text: Comparative advantage, rather than absolute advantage, is the basis for gains from trade because

generalfeedback.text: Absolute advantage compares output per worker. Comparative advantage compares opportunity cost. Trade can benefit both sides when those opportunity costs differ.

answer.text: a country must be absolutely more productive in every good before it can export
trade only helps the country that is larger in every industry
a country gains by specialising in the good with the lower opportunity cost, even if it is less productive in both goods

questiontext.text: Free trade can let a country consume

answer.text: at a point that violates opportunity cost inside the trading partner as well, by definition
only inside its production possibility frontier, with no exception

questiontext.text: International trade is

answer.text: the same thing as the national debt

always raises real income in proportion to the index
